title: Native Execution Engine fallback: the four trigger tiers
purpose: Native execution fallback tiers. Tier one whole query; Tier two operator; Tier three expression; Tier four data type; How to detect fallback.
accessibleSummary: Native execution fallback tiers. Tier one whole query; Tier two operator; Tier three expression; Tier four data type; How to detect fallback.
longDescription: Native execution fallback tiers. Tier one whole query; Tier two operator; Tier three expression; Tier four data type; How to detect fallback.

nodes.label: Tier 1 — whole query falls back
nodes.summary: Streaming, ANSI mode and JSON/XML sources force the entire query onto the JVM.
nodes.detail: Streaming, ANSI mode and JSON/XML sources force the entire query onto the JVM.
nodes.whyItMatters: Streaming, ANSI mode and JSON/XML sources force the entire query onto the JVM.

evidence.note: Structured streaming and ANSI SQL mode always execute on JVM Spark, and JSON/XML source formats are not accelerated.

drill.example: A structured streaming job gains nothing from the native engine regardless of configuration.
failureModes: Sizing a streaming cluster against native benchmarks over-promises throughput.

nodes.label: Tier 2 — one operator falls back
nodes.summary: An operator with no Velox equivalent runs on the JVM with conversions either side.
nodes.detail: An operator with no Velox equivalent runs on the JVM with conversions either side.
nodes.whyItMatters: An operator with no Velox equivalent runs on the JVM with conversions either side.

evidence.note: An unsupported operator causes the affected query segment to fall back to standard JVM Spark.
Fallback triggers form four tiers, and identifying the tier is the first diagnostic step.

processing: Match each operator against Velox support
drill.example: An unsupported window frame runs on the JVM while the surrounding scan and aggregate stay native.
failureModes: An unsupported operator in the middle of a plan pays conversion cost twice.

nodes.label: Tier 3 — one expression, whole operator lost
nodes.summary: One unsupported expression or UDF drops its whole enclosing operator to the JVM.
nodes.detail: One unsupported expression or UDF drops its whole enclosing operator to the JVM.
nodes.whyItMatters: One unsupported expression or UDF drops its whole enclosing operator to the JVM.

evidence.note: A single unsupported expression or Python UDF drops the whole enclosing operator to JVM execution.

processing: Detect an unsupported function or UDF
outputs: The enclosing operator demoted to JVM
drill.example: One Python UDF in a projection removes native execution for that entire projection.
failureModes: The performance loss is attributed to the UDF alone, understating the true cost.

nodes.label: Tier 4 — data types
nodes.summary: Deeply nested and complex data types push execution back to the JVM.
nodes.detail: Deeply nested and complex data types push execution back to the JVM.
nodes.whyItMatters: Deeply nested and complex data types push execution back to the JVM.

evidence.note: Deeply nested structs and maps, and complex-type manipulation, trigger fallback.

processing: Detect deeply nested or complex types
outputs: JVM execution for the affected work
drill.example: Repeated manipulation of a nested struct in a hot path keeps returning execution to the JVM.
failureModes: Nesting and unnesting repeatedly multiplies conversion boundaries.

nodes.label: Read the plan
nodes.summary: Plan suffixes reveal which operators genuinely executed natively.
nodes.detail: Plan suffixes reveal which operators genuinely executed natively.
nodes.whyItMatters: Plan suffixes reveal which operators genuinely executed natively.

evidence.note: Native operators carry suffixes such as *Transformer, confirming what actually ran natively.

processing: Inspect operator suffixes and conversion nodes
outputs: Evidence of native or JVM execution
drill.example: A plan showing only standard operator names with the engine enabled proves total fallback.
failureModes: Reading only the initial plan misses AQE's final adaptive plan.

nodes.label: Spark Advisor, inline
nodes.summary: The Spark Advisor alerts on fallback in real time as a notebook cell runs.
nodes.detail: The Spark Advisor alerts on fallback in real time as a notebook cell runs.
nodes.whyItMatters: The Spark Advisor alerts on fallback in real time as a notebook cell runs.

evidence.note: The Fabric Spark Advisor surfaces real-time alerts during notebook cell execution when execution falls back to JVM-based Spark.

drill.example: A cell reports fallback immediately, before the job has even finished.
failureModes: Alerts are per cell, so a scheduled job needs the post-run Diagnostics route instead.

nodes.label: Diagnostics pane, post-run
nodes.summary: The Diagnostics pane names the root cause of fallback after the run.
nodes.detail: The Diagnostics pane names the root cause of fallback after the run.
nodes.whyItMatters: The Diagnostics pane names the root cause of fallback after the run.

evidence.note: Whether an operator executed natively can be confirmed via the Spark UI.

processing: Read the fallback report and root cause
drill.example: The root-cause view names the specific expression that forced the JVM path.
failureModes: Post-run only, so it cannot shorten the feedback loop during development.
